lede: Mountain Village Council meets Wednesday with a resolution that sets the appreciation cap on deed-restricted units — the fine print that determines whether affordable housing actually stays affordable for the next buyer, not just the first one. Also Wednesday, HARC takes a hard look at the Shandoka Lot redevelopment on Black Bear Road, Ouray County holds three public hearings including a full repeal of a land-use code section, and the BOCC sits as the Housing Authority to work through regional affordable-housing compliance at a moment when those finances are under strain.

notable.stake: HARC decides whether to retroactively approve unpermitted Elks Lodge pergola.
Preliminary large-scale HARC review of major new construction at Shandoka Lot.
Vote on 2027 campground and shower fee increases, including a 25% shower rate hike.
BOCC reviews housing authority compliance and holds a public hearing on land use.
Three public hearings: land-use code repeal, SUP amendment, and exception application.
Public hearings on special event liquor permits for multiple upcoming community events.
Council votes on appreciation cap that controls long-term affordability of deed-restricted units.
First formal review of school district employee housing proposal on public school site.
